name: Scale SWE-bench Pro

measures.reason: Directly measures end-to-end repository issue resolution, bug fixes, feature requests, and multi-file changes across real software codebases.

methodology: Agents receive a repository issue and codebase context, produce git patches, and solutions are graded pass/fail against unit and regression test suites.
harness: SWE-agent scaffold or vendor agent scaffold in Docker sandbox environments.
tools: Terminal shell, file read/write, patch application, python test execution.
context_profile: Full multi-file repository context (averaging 107.4 LOC modified across 4.1 files per task instance).
contamination_notes: Sourced from copyleft (GPL) and private commercial codebases to minimize training data exposure.
limitations: Contested validity: OpenAI audit (2026-07-08) indicated 27.4-34.1% broken tasks on public set; version consistency is critical.

name: Scale SWE-bench Pro V2
locator: Scale SWE-bench Pro V2 Full leaderboard and evaluation protocol

measures.reason: Refined SWE-bench Pro dataset with network-locked execution protocol and sanitized task instances.

methodology: Network-isolated task execution grading multi-file issue resolution against verified test suites on filtered 642-task split.
harness: mini-swe-agent / Codex scaffold with network-locked execution container.
tools: Isolated container shell, filesystem tools, test runners.
context_profile: Full repository tree across 41 repositories with strict network cutoff.
contamination_notes: Updated sanitization over original public split to filter broken or leaked instances.
limitations: Not directly comparable to V1 public split (731 tasks); scores must not be pooled across versions.

name: SWE-Lancer IC

measures.reason: Evaluates complex freelance software engineering tasks with economic value ($1M prize pool equivalent), verified by end-to-end integration tests.

methodology: Agents are assigned real-world commercial freelance Upwork tasks (bug fixes, feature additions, full-stack components) in dedicated per-task Docker containers.
harness: OpenAI Frontier Evals / preparedness harness with dockerized per-task environments.
tools: Bash shell, full filesystem access, language runtime toolchains.
languages: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, PHP
context_profile: Full commercial freelance repositories, multi-component systems, frontend/backend integration.
contamination_notes: Proprietary client repositories sampled directly from Upwork contracts, verified offline.
limitations: High resource cost per task evaluation (~14GB Docker image per task); frontier model public results stopped being updated by OpenAI after Nov 2025.

name: RepoProbe

measures.reason: Measures repository-level architectural comprehension, business logic understanding, and cross-module reasoning without allowing immediate patch trial-and-error.

methodology: 500 open-ended architectural and implementation questions derived from real GitHub Discussions across 50 repositories, evaluated against human-expert checklist verification protocols.
harness: RepoProbe benchmark runner with checklist grading.
tools: Repository file tree inspection, code search, document reading.
context_profile: Complete repository codebase and architecture documentation.
contamination_notes: Derived from GitHub Discussions (natural developer questions rather than code commits) to avoid synthetic leakage.
limitations: Currently evaluated against older frontier models in the paper (up to GPT-5.4 / Opus 4.6); live evaluations for the 2026-09 frozen working ladder are not yet published.

name: ArchBench
locator: 2026 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Software Architecture Companion (ICSA-C)

measures.reason: Evaluates generative AI models on software architecture tasks including architectural design, trade-off reasoning, and system decomposition.

methodology: Standardized architecture task specifications requiring decomposition, quality attribute trade-off analysis, and component-connector design generation.
tools: Prompt-based and structured architectural specification inputs.
languages: Architecture description languages, UML/plantUML, structured Markdown, multi-language implementations
context_profile: System architecture requirements and structural context.
contamination_notes: Curated architectural problems designed specifically for the benchmark.
limitations: Academic benchmark with low public model coverage for the latest 2026 frontier ladder rungs.

name: AACR-Bench

measures.reason: Directly measures repository-level context-aware automated code review capabilities, defect detection, precision, and recall.

methodology: 200 real pull requests sampled across 50 active open-source projects; models generate review comments scored against expert-verified ground truth reviews.
tools: PR diff viewing, repository context navigation.
languages: C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust, C#, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby (10 languages)
context_profile: PR diff plus surrounding repository context and dependency graph.
contamination_notes: Expert-filtered and verified human review comments from active projects.
limitations: Published paper evaluates Claude 4.5 Sonnet, GPT-5.2, DeepSeek V3.2; no public leaderboard rows yet for current frozen rungs (Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6, Gemini 3.8).

name: Terminal-Bench
locator: Terminal-Bench 4.0 release and BenchLeader aa_terminalbench_40 board

measures.reason: Tests end-to-end agent execution, command-line problem solving, build troubleshooting, server deployment, and debugging in a realistic Linux terminal.

methodology: Autonomous agents interact with a full sandboxed Linux CLI environment to complete complex system-administration, development, and ML operational tasks.
harness: Harbor Terminal-Bench execution harness and Artificial Analysis evaluation setup.
tools: Bash shell, CLI utilities, standard Linux tools, process control.
languages: Bash, Python, C++, Go, Rust, System configurations
context_profile: Interactive terminal environment with persistent filesystem and network isolation.
contamination_notes: Continuously updated task sets with regular version bumps (2.1 -> Hard -> 4.0) to avoid memorization.
limitations: Significant variance between vendor-reported harnesses and independent (AA) standardized runs (up to 7-10 points difference).

name: Terminal-Bench
locator: Terminal-Bench 2.1 leaderboard on tbench.ai and BenchLeader aa_terminalbench_21

measures.reason: Measures autonomous terminal task execution across early standard set.

methodology: Sandboxed Linux terminal task suite evaluated on resolution pass rate.
contamination_notes: Early benchmark iteration with partial saturation at frontier tier.
limitations: Saturation near top tier (>85% resolution by top models); superseded by 4.0 for frontier discrimination.

name: Terminal-Bench Hard

measures.reason: Measures complex, multi-step debugging and long-horizon troubleshooting under strict terminal execution constraints.

methodology: Curated hard subset of Terminal-Bench tasks requiring deep system diagnosis and multi-stage repairs.
context_profile: Sandboxed Linux system with degraded components.
contamination_notes: Carefully selected hard tasks to resist automated heuristic shortcuts.
limitations: Small sample size (28 tasks); higher variance per run.

name: LiveCodeBench
locator: arXiv:2403.07974; livecodebench.github.io leaderboard and Vals AI window

measures.reason: Evaluates algorithmic problem solving, code generation, execution prediction, self-repair, and test generation on contest problems.

methodology: Continuously collects new competitive programming problems from LeetCode, AtCoder, and Codeforces; models are evaluated across generation, execution, and repair modes.
harness: LiveCodeBench execution harness with automated test-suite verification.
tools: Pure code generation and input/output test execution.
context_profile: Self-contained algorithmic problem statement with input/output format and constraints.
contamination_notes: Continuous time-stamped problem ingestion ensures evaluation only on problems released after model training cutoffs.
limitations: Does not reflect repository-level multi-file architecture or engineering constraints; algorithmic coding skill does not transfer directly to multi-file codebase maintenance.

name: Aider Polyglot Benchmark

measures.reason: Directly measures the model's ability to take existing code files and specification instructions, output correctly formatted diff/edit blocks, and satisfy unit tests across 6 languages.

methodology: 225 challenging Exercism-based programming exercises across 6 languages; model outputs edit blocks that Aider applies to repository files and verifies with unit test suites.
harness: Aider benchmark dockerized harness (Pass@2 test protocol).
tools: Diff/edit block formatting, patch application, unit test execution.
languages: C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust
context_profile: Existing source code files and exercise instructions.
contamination_notes: Standard Exercism exercises with complex problem variations.
limitations: Third-party runs show large score disparities against original maintainer boards; harness provenance must be carefully tracked.

name: SWE-Lancer Manager

measures.reason: Serves as an indirect proxy for engineering judgment and proposal evaluation; models review competing implementation pitches and select the optimal design against human engineering manager decisions.

methodology: Models are presented with real freelance engineering job proposals and technical solutions, requiring them to critique, evaluate trade-offs, and select the winning proposal matching manager ground truth.
languages: Natural language technical proposals and architecture descriptions
context_profile: Freelance client requirements and competing engineering proposals.
contamination_notes: Sourced from proprietary Upwork manager workflows.
limitations: Proxy only (cannot exceed WEAK status per PROTO-DEC-0084); does not test adversarial code audit, security vulnerability discovery, or protocol verification.

name: RuleBench / Specification Compliance Suite
locator: Software architecture and rule instruction dataset

measures.reason: Evaluates general rule following on text instructions.

methodology: Instruction and rule following evaluations on synthetic constraints.
limitations: Does not evaluate repository specification adherence, protocol rulebooks, or multi-file architectural constraints.
exclusion_reason: Public rule/documentation compliance datasets do not evaluate multi-file software engineering repository rules, architectural invariant compliance, or agent workflow guardrails; local evaluation only per contract.

name: MultiDoc-Synthesis Suite
locator: Multi-document QA and cross-document synthesis dataset

measures.reason: Evaluates cross-document synthesis on general NLP texts.

methodology: Cross-document question answering and information consolidation.
context_profile: Multiple research papers or text documents.
limitations: Evaluates natural language summarization rather than multi-document repository architecture design or cross-file coordination.
exclusion_reason: Public multi-document summarization/QA datasets test generic natural language synthesis rather than multi-document repository architecture design, cross-file change coordination, or protocol ledger consolidation; local evaluation only per contract.
